title: Post-Eviction Retention, Faithfulness, and Refusal Control
formal_question: After document context is evicted from the prompt, how do memory-only (P1) and hybrid retrieval (P2) perform? Does P2 improve citation faithfulness over BM25 RAG (B2)?

audit_findings.claim_in_round2_report: When context is evicted, P1 maintains 0.420 F1 while non-memory baselines collapse to 0; Refusal Gate achieves 95.0% or 96.0% refusal accuracy on unanswerable queries.

discrepancies_identified.refusal_accuracy_discrepancy: Round 2 reports claimed 95.0% and 96.0% refusal accuracy. The actual raw result in rq3_raw_results.json across all 3 seeds is strictly 76.0% (19/25 unanswerable + 19/25 insufficient evidence = 38/50 = 76.0%). False refusal rate on answerable items is strictly 0.0% (0/50).
discrepancies_identified.f1_score_discrepancy: Round 2 reports cited P1 F1 = 0.420 and P2 F1 = 0.828. In the frozen benchmark table 03_rq3_summary.csv, the context-evicted token F1 for P1 is 0.0753 and for P2 is 0.1596 (evaluated on Vietnamese 100 items). The 0.828 number came from a different exploratory run, NOT the locked benchmark.
discrepancies_identified.memory_refusal_limitation: Neither P1 nor B5 (memory-only models) possesses intrinsic refusal capability (both score 0.0% correct refusal and 100.0% false answer). All refusal safety in P2 originates from the non-parametric retrieval scoring and RefusalController thresholds.

audit_findings.valid_scientific_findings: Direct document context removal causes prompt baseline B1 to collapse completely (F1=0.0048, 100% hallucination). P2 Gated Hybrid reliably prevents hallucination (76% correct refusal, 0% false refusal) and achieves the highest verified citation faithfulness (98.92% vs 95.70% for B2).
